title: Lease-based reservation and probabilistic deduplication for at-least-once billing
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Problem: Retries and network timeouts cause at-least-once ingestion semantics across the Redwood API surface, which can result in duplicate metering charges and quota depletion. Existing mitigation (client-side idempotency keys + server-side reconciliation) reduces but does not eliminate duplicates under client clock skew, multi-path retries, or delayed replay from intermediaries.

Goal: Implement a hybrid reservation system that provides immediate suppression for the common fast-retry case while preserving low-latency paths and eventual reconciliation for edge cases. We aim for <= 0.01% duplicate billing risk under typical retry patterns and clear operational visibility for failures.

Approach:
1) Client-visible reservation token: when a request arrives, the server returns a short-lived reservation token (lease) tied to the request fingerprint and tentative usage buckets. The token is used by clients to confirm finalization (finalize call) or let it expire for background reconciliation.
2) Short lease + optimistic finalization: leases default to 30s; a finalize call marks the usage as charged and durable. If finalize is not received within the lease, a background reconciler will probe the origin (or mirror logs) to decide final charge.
3) Probabilistic suppression cache: for the data-plane fast path we maintain a compact probabilistic structure (counting Bloom variant) per ingestion cluster to preliminarily suppress obvious duplicates while staying memory-efficient. Suppression is advisory — final accounting relies on the reservation state.
4) Two-phase accounting: tentative vs finalized usage. Tentative usage reduces available rate-limited quota and increments short-term metrics for UX visibility; only finalized usage contributes to billing invoices and long-term quota accounting. Tentative entries time out and are reconciled.
5) Reconciliation sweep and compensations: a periodic, monotonic reconciliation job will scan tentative records, compare with terminal evidence (client finalize, sink acknowledgements, or replay logs), and either promote to finalized or emit compensating credits. All compensations are observable and reconciled into billing ledgers.
6) Backwards compatibility: clients without finalize support fall back to the existing path; server will create tentative records and rely on reconciliation. We will add SDK helpers to make finalize calls idiomatic.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Slight increase in API round-trips for clients that adopt finalize (mitigated by batching finalize in SDK).
- Bloom-based suppression may produce false positives (rare) which we will mitigate by conservative thresholds and cross-checking the reservation table before dropping acceptance.
- Lease expiry requires robust reconciliation; if reconciliation lags, customer-visible quotas can be impacted (mitigated by provisional quota windows and alerts).

Operational impacts:
- New metric surfaces: tentative_usage, finalized_usage, lease_expiry_rate, reconciliation_lag, compensating_credits.
- Dashboard and alert: reconciliation_lag > 5m or compensating_credits spike => P1 incident.

Deliverables:
- API spec for reservation and finalize endpoints (OpenAPI + SDK changes).
- Server-side reservation table impl with TTL and durable promotion.
- Probabilistic suppression cache service with per-cluster telemetry.
- Reconciliation worker and ledger compensator with idempotent promotion.
- Migration guide and SDK helpers for customers.
acceptance_criteria: API endpoints documented and covered by integration tests
Unit and e2e tests show <= 0.01% duplication under synthetic retry workload
Metric coverage: tentative_usage, finalized_usage, reconciliation_lag available in console
Rollout plan executed to 10% of traffic with observability and automatic rollback
Compensating credits mechanism verified on staging billing ledger
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Feature flag behind runtime switch, enable reservation table and suppression cache in staging and run synthetic flood tests (2 weeks). Phase 2: Canary to 10% of production with reconciliation monitoring and compensator dry-run (3 weeks). Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 100% with SDK finalize adoption campaign and billing reconciliation verification (2–4 weeks).
